chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Jazz at the Philharmonic, Sugar Ray Robinson's club and the Chez Sassy
summary: After work musicians gather at Sugar Ray Robinson's club, and a Paris club is named after Sarah.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: During that particular time, Jazz at the Philharmonic came over with Oscar Peterson and Ray Brown, Ella Fitzgerald. At that particular time, the boxer, Sugar Ray Robinson, had a club over there. This is where we all congregated after we got off of work. It turned out to be a very happy time.

After finishing that engagement at this club... Someone had opened a club over there, and they gave the club a name... As a matter of fact, they named the club after Sarah. The club was called the Chez Sassy, I think. I thought that was a rather unique thing, because we'd only been in Paris a short while, and all of a sudden there's a club there with Sarah's name. Anyway, I don't remember how long we played there, but
we were there until we left Paris, which I think was about two more weeks.
